Description: A major city on the west bank of the Euphrates at one of the chief crossings between Mesopotamia and the west, at modern Jerablus on the Turkey-Syria border. In turn an independent trading kingdom, the seat of Hittite viceroys, the capital of a Neo-Hittite state, and an Assyrian provincial centre, it guarded the route every empire travelling between Mesopotamia and the Levant had to use. George Smith identified Jerablus as Carchemish in 1876; British Museum excavations under D. G. Hogarth, C. Leonard Woolley, and T. E. Lawrence (1911-1914) exposed the citadel walls and gates, temples, and processions of Hittite reliefs and statues, and renewed Turkish work has continued in the 21st century.
HistoricalPeriod: Bronze Age to Neo-Assyrian, 3rd millennium to 605 BC
Interpretations: Scholars agree Jerablus is biblical Carchemish; the identification, made in 1876, was confirmed by excavation. The battle itself left no single excavated battlefield layer that can be pointed to, and none is claimed — the entry is for the city whose crossing made the battle possible and whose fall Jeremiah dated.
RelatedEvents: Fall of Jerusalem and the Exile
BiblicalSignificance: Carchemish is where the ancient world turned. In 605 BC Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon destroyed Pharaoh Necho's Egyptian army there (Jeremiah 46:2; 2 Chronicles 35:20), a victory that gave Babylon control of Syria and Palestine, Judah included, and opened the road to Jerusalem's fall. Isaiah had already listed Carchemish among the kingdoms Assyria overran (Isaiah 10:9). The Babylonian Chronicle's account of the battle matches Jeremiah's dating to the fourth year of Jehoiakim, anchoring the prophet's ministry in a dated, excavated place.
ArtifactDate: Hittite and Neo-Hittite city; Assyrian provincial capital from 717 BC; battle of 605 BC
CurrentLocation: In situ, Turkey (citadel and inner city on the Turkish side; access restricted by a military zone)
DateDiscovered: Identified by George Smith, 1876; British Museum excavations 1878-1881 and 1911-1914 (Hogarth, Woolley, T. E. Lawrence)
DiscoveryLocation: Jerablus / Karkamis, on the west bank of the Euphrates, Turkey-Syria border
